title: Low Tide: Staff Gauge
statement: Mara let the post be colonised and read the barnacles as a tide mark. I made the reading official. The post now carries a staff gauge up its seaward face, alternating pale and dark bands of equal height with a tick at every joint, so that any morning's water can be read off it in units nobody has named. Two lines are painted across: a red one at the top of the barnacle band, which is where the sea usually stops, and a blue one at today's water, which is lower. In the corner a card records the readings, blank lines with the two colours marked and a dashed stamp. The weed and the barnacles are untouched; they were the first gauge, and mine is only a copy of theirs in paint. The next hand can take the next reading, or let the barnacles cover the numbers.
process: I kept Mara's parent exactly, the shallow flood, the post, the barnacles, the kelp skirt and the reflected buoy, and painted a staff gauge of fifteen alternating bands with ticks up the post's face, a red datum line at the barnacle mark and a blue line at the present water, with a reading card in the upper right joined to the gauge by a dotted leader.
